While these intervals encompass a wide range of plausible outcomes under expected conditions, certain extreme or unpredictable events could push the actual value far outside these boundaries. These "tail risks" include sudden, significant economic downturns or booms, unexpected policy changes from central banks or governments, major geopolitical conflicts, large-scale natural disasters, or unprecedented technological disruptions. Such events, though unlikely, can fundamentally alter the underlying assumptions of the forecast, leading to rapid and substantial deviations that fall beyond the scope of typical market volatility and the expected range of our 90% confidence.
